reasons: The frozen coordinatewise weak-unconfoundedness condition does not control evaluation at the random dose. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element rules out the diagonal-null-set witness and supplies the conditional-product calculation used in the causal bridge. It remains compatible with the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower construction by taking one independent common uniform random variable and thresholding it at the continuous conditional mean. (not crux: This is a standard structural exogeneity condition. It does not assume the ADRF formula, analytic identification, a stability modulus, a rate, or the lower-bound separation, and it leaves every measurement-error condition unchanged.)

The directed structural response-surface condition and the already accepted causal-mean continuity condition must be member properties of the same quantitative class used by identification, the upper theorem, and the lower experiment.

verdict.note: High-effort adjudication: structural exogenous response surface is faithful, closes the random-diagonal defect, and is compatible with fixed-nuisance Bernoulli alternatives; model-class wiring is necessary.
